newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS DOWNHILL, GOETSCHL CLAIMS SEASON TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS DOWNHILL, GOETSCHL CLAIMS SEASON TITLE.

text.p: Overall champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden capped a dream season by winning her first downhill Wednesday at the World Cup Finals, while Austrian Renate Goetschl made a daring last run to win the downhill title.

Wiberg, who became the first Scandinavian woman to win the overall championship on the strength of four slalom and two Super-G victories, roared down the 2,626-meter Vail Mountain course in one minute, 43.28 seconds for a narrow victory.
"I can not believe it," said Wiberg, who was fastest by three-hundredths of a second. "Wow!"

Goetschl, the 24th and last skier to race, needed a big finish to jump from third to first in the final downhill standings. The 21-year-old Austrian came through, clocking 1:43.31 to tie German veteran Katja Seizinger for second.
Goetschl leapfrogged over Swiss Heidi Zurbriggen, fifth in the race, and Russian Warwara Zelenskaja, a dismal 18th, in the standings to claim the season title.
Zurbriggen clocked 1:43.78 to finish behind fourth-placed Italian Isolde Kostner in 1:43.61.
World downhill champion Hilary Lindh of the United States finished ninth in 1:44.15..

"It was very tight with Heidi," said Goetschl, who would have lost the crown to Zurbriggen if she had been one-hundredth of a second slower. "The downhill is the queen discipline of the World Cup. It's a sensation."

Goetschl, who won a downhill at Vail earlier this season, finished with 483 points to 466 for Zurbriggen. Zelenskaja was third in the standings with 423 and Wiberg took fourth place with her season-ending victory.

The win by Wiberg made up for a bitter disappointment in Vail three years ago when a downhill crash at the Finals ruined her chances for the overall title. This triumph also made the Swede the only active woman racer to own wins in all four Alpine World Cup disciplines.

"It's amazing to become the only one with wins in all four events," said a jubilant Wiberg. "It's unbelievable. If I would have dreamed about that at the start of my career I would not have believed it."
Wiberg, 26, said the crash near the bottom of the course that cost her the overall crown to Swiss Vreni Schneider at the 1994 Finals had helped her achieve victory this time.
"I was more focused because of that crash. I knew I couldn't make any mistakes," she said.
Goetschl said she did not realise she had grabbed her first career World Cup season title when she first glimpsed her time at the finish.
"I thought I had to win the race to get the title," said Goetschl, who won the combined event at this year's World Championships at Sestriere, Italy.
"When I saw I was second, I thought I blew it. Then I saw that Wiberg was in the lead and I knew I had won."
Zelenskaja, trying to become the first Russian to win a World Cup title, entered the finale with a scant two-point lead over Zurbriggen at 423-421, with Goetschl at 403.
"I was nervous, like always, nothing special," said Zelenskaja. "It was just not my run. I made mistakes. But it's okay, I have a lot more years and I will be fighting for the top place."
